name: How do you know if your bathroom is big enough for a walk-in shower?

mainEntity.name: How do you tell whether a small bathroom in Los Angeles is big enough for a comfortable walk-in shower after removing the tub?
mainEntity.text: How do you tell whether a small bathroom in Los Angeles is big enough for a comfortable walk-in shower after removing the tub?

acceptedAnswer.text: Whether a bathroom is big enough depends on the layout, not only the square footage. A tub-to-shower conversion may work in a compact bathroom if the shower footprint fits the available alcove and there is still enough space to move around the vanity, toilet, and entry door. Homeowners should check shower dimensions, door clearance, and how the new shower will affect traffic flow. In small bathrooms, a fixed glass panel or sliding door can save space compared with a swinging door. If the goal is better accessibility, a wider opening and low-threshold entry may matter more than maximum enclosure size. A contractor can help confirm what fits before design decisions are made. It is also smart to think about storage, lighting, and ventilation, because a small room can feel cramped if those are not addressed. The best conversion balances comfort, function, and moisture control instead of simply replacing the tub with the biggest possible shower.
acceptedAnswer.description: A bathroom can be large enough if the new shower still meets practical clearances, door swing needs, and code requirements. The key is not just total room size, but whether the shower footprint, entry path, and nearby fixtures will still function comfortably.
